figs.name: distributed-control-system-levels-block-diagram
figs.alt: distributed control system block diagram with field devices, controllers, bus and operator levels
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog showing DCS levels 0 to 4: field devices, controllers with I/O racks on a high speed bus, operator stations, production control and plant management.

figs.name: distributed-control-system-signal-flowchart
figs.alt: flowchart of a signal moving from sensor to controller, operator station and back to a valve
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog tracing a DCS loop: the sensor reading rises through the I/O rack and controller to the operator station, then the output returns to the actuator.
figs.after_h2: Layers of a Distributed Control System (DCS)
figs.svg:
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" viewBox="0 0 800 610" width="100%" font-family="Arial, Helvetica, sans-serif">
<title>Flowchart of a measurement travelling through the DCS levels and back to a valve</title>
<rect width="800" height="610" fill="#ffffff"/>
<defs><marker id="ah" viewBox="0 0 10 10" refX="9" refY="5" markerWidth="7" markerHeight="7" orient="auto-start-reverse"><path d="M0 0L10 5L0 10z" fill="#1a2b4a"/></marker></defs>
<text x="400.0" y="34" font-size="24" fill="#0c4a6e" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">How a Signal Moves Through the DCS</text>
<rect x="40" y="450" width="300" height="96" rx="10" fill="#f0f9ff" stroke="#0369a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="190.0" y="480.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Level 0</text>
<text x="190.0" y="503.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Sensor measures</text>
<text x="190.0" y="526.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">temperature or flow</text>
<line x1="190" y1="450" x2="190" y2="406" stroke="#0c4a6e" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<rect x="40" y="310" width="300" height="96" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0369a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="190.0" y="340.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Level 1</text>
<text x="190.0" y="363.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">I/O rack reads it,</text>
<text x="190.0" y="386.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">controller runs the loop</text>
<line x1="190" y1="310" x2="190" y2="266" stroke="#0c4a6e" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<rect x="40" y="170" width="300" height="96" rx="10" fill="#f0f9ff" stroke="#0369a1" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="190.0" y="200.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Level 2</text>
<text x="190.0" y="223.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Operator station</text>
<text x="190.0" y="246.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">shows value, alarms</text>
<rect x="460" y="170" width="300" height="96" rx="10" fill="#f0f9ff" stroke="#0c4a6e" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="610.0" y="200.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Level 2</text>
<text x="610.0" y="223.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Operator changes</text>
<text x="610.0" y="246.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">setpoint if needed</text>
<line x1="610" y1="266" x2="610" y2="310" stroke="#0c4a6e" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<rect x="460" y="310" width="300" height="96" rx="10" fill="#ffffff" stroke="#0c4a6e" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="610.0" y="340.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Level 1</text>
<text x="610.0" y="363.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Controller sends</text>
<text x="610.0" y="386.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">new output</text>
<line x1="610" y1="406" x2="610" y2="450" stroke="#0c4a6e" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<rect x="460" y="450" width="300" height="96" rx="10" fill="#f0f9ff" stroke="#0c4a6e" stroke-width="2"/>
<text x="610.0" y="480.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="bold" text-anchor="middle">Level 0</text>
<text x="610.0" y="503.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Actuator moves</text>
<text x="610.0" y="526.95" font-size="17" fill="#1a2b4a" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">the valve</text>
<line x1="340" y1="218" x2="458" y2="218" stroke="#0c4a6e" stroke-width="3" marker-end="url(#ah)"/>
<polyline points="610,546 610,566 190,566 190,550" fill="none" stroke="#0c4a6e" stroke-width="2.5" marker-end="url(#ah)" stroke-dasharray="6 5"/>
<text x="400" y="92" font-size="17" fill="#4b5563" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">Levels 3 and 4 watch production and set schedules,</text>
<text x="400" y="118" font-size="17" fill="#4b5563" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">they do not drive field devices directly</text>
<text x="400" y="592" font-size="17" fill="#4b5563" font-weight="normal" text-anchor="middle">process responds, loop repeats</text>
</svg>

figs.name: distributed-control-system-advantages-infographic
figs.alt: distributed control system advantages and loop count comparison of a small plant and a refinery
figs.caption: Diagram by Instrumentation Blog comparing a wastewater plant with about a dozen loops to a refinery with nearly 10,000, plus six DCS advantages listed in the article.
figs.after_h2: What Makes the DCS so Important?
